name: Interior
summary: Everything inside the cockpit that is not primary safety structure: stripping the shell, dash and switch panels, pedal-area floor, driver cooling, mirrors, door cards and ballast. The goal is a light, clean, serviceable cockpit with nothing loose and every control reachable while belted.
overview:
A bare-chassis build starts by stripping the Gen 6 shell of all trim, seats, SRS components and asphalt deadener so the cage and seat mounts can be welded to clean metal. The factory IP cross-car beam can be retained to locate the steering column and EPS, with a lightweight race dash panel on top; or the column is hung from the cage dash bar.

The cockpit is laid out around the seated driver: display above the wheel, switch panel and kill/fire controls in the center stack within reach of the belted driver, heel plate and dead pedal in the footwell, cool-suit cooler and fire bottle low on the passenger floor. Door cards close the gutted doors around the door bars.

Ballast must be through-bolted with backing plates (never strapped) and placed low and inboard to help cross-weight.
buildNotes: Strip and de-deadener before cage work.
Decide factory beam vs. cage column support before the dash bar is placed.
Weld all interior mounting tabs to the cage before paint.
Install dash, panels, cooling and mirrors after electrical harness routing.
Add ballast last during corner weighting.
